title: Your camera has been able to do this for a year

slides.headline: Your phone camera has been able to do this //for about a year. //[[gold]]Nobody told you.[[/gold]]
Models started watching video and listening at the same time
slides.body: Not "take a photo, wait, read a paragraph back". A live stream, both directions, while you're still talking.

slides.headline: It mostly got used for demos
slides.body: Impressive on a stage, nowhere near your actual Tuesday. The useful version is boring: point it at a thing, ask about the thing.

items.text: Reading something too small to read
Naming a part you can't name
Choosing between two things in your hands
Working out dinner from what's actually in the fridge

slides.headline: The unglamorous test
slides.before: Identifies the Eiffel Tower. Describes a sunset. Reads a QR code you could have scanned.
slides.after: Tells you which of these two tins has less salt, while you're stood in the aisle holding both.

slides.headline: It needs to see and hear to do it
slides.body: Camera and voice stream to Google's Gemini while a session is open. Argus says so before you start, and nothing happens when you're not connected.

slides.headline: Try it on the next thing you can't identify
slides.fineprint: No account, no password. Delete everything from inside the app.

caption.tiktok:
Phones have been able to do this for about a year and it mostly got used for stage demos. The useful version is unglamorous: point it at the thing you can't read, can't name, or can't choose between, and ask.

Free on iPhone — search “My Argus” on the App Store (the gold ring).
caption.instagram:
Live camera + live voice models have existed for roughly a year. Almost all of it got spent identifying landmarks on stage.

The actually useful version is much more boring — which tin has less salt, what is this part called, what can I make with this. That's what Argus is for.

It does need to see and hear while you're connected, and it tells you that up front.

Send this to someone who thinks AI apps are all the same.

Free on iPhone — link in bio.
